SYNTHETIC: an invented decision written for the corpus builder tests. No real person, state or case.

Human Rights Committee
Views under article 5(4) of the Optional Protocol, communication No. 9999/2099
Author: Orla Venk (invented)
State party: Republic of Talmora (invented)

Facts as submitted by the author

2.1 The author is a journalist and the editor of an independent news portal in the capital. On 3 March 2099 she was arrested at her office and charged with disseminating false information about the regional water authority.

2.2 She was held in police custody for five days before she was first brought before a judge, who ordered her pretrial detention without hearing her lawyer.

2.3 Her lawyer was not allowed to attend the remand hearing, and she met him for the first time two
weeks after her arrest.

2.4 At trial the court refused to hear the two defence witnesses named by the author, stating that their evidence was “not relevant to the charge”.

2.5 The court of appeal upheld the conviction in a short decision.

Consideration of the merits

7.1 The Committee notes the State party's statement that the author was detained under its criminal procedure code.

7.2 The Committee considers that the facts before it disclose a violation of article 9(3) of the Covenant.

7.3 The Committee finds that the refusal to hear the defence witnesses violated article 14(3)(e) of the Covenant.

7.4 The Committee considers that the facts before it disclose a violation of article 9(3) of the Covenant.
